final_briefs.title: Windows Loudness Equalization, reverse-engineered and ported to PipeWire
final_briefs.description: **Linux audio now gets Windows‑style loudness equalization via PipeWire.** The project reverse‑engineers the Windows feature and implements it as a low‑latency filter for PipeWire, giving Linux desktops a proven volume‑balancing filter without extra hardware.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Bringing Windows‑style loudness equalization to PipeWire gives Linux audio stacks a proven, low‑latency volume‑balancing filter without extra hardware.
final_briefs.who_cares: Audio engineers, Linux desktop developers, and anyone building media playback or recording apps on Linux.

final_briefs.title: Bypassing iOS Safari's 60 FPS Limit to Build Web Applications That Feel Native
final_briefs.description: **You can break the 60 fps ceiling on iOS Safari by offloading scroll handling to the compositor.** By using the compositor thread for scrolling, touch and pointer events are no longer throttled to 60 Hz, enabling smoother, native‑like interactions in mobile web apps.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: By offloading scroll handling to the compositor you can break the 60 fps ceiling on iOS Safari and deliver truly native‑feel web interactions.
final_briefs.who_cares: Front‑end engineers building high‑performance mobile web apps, especially those using React, Vue, or Svelte.

final_briefs.title: OlliteRT: Android LLM Server in 3 Steps
final_briefs.description: **Turn an old Android phone into a private, offline LLM inference server.** OlliteRT uses Google’s LiteRT‑LM runtime to run models on the device’s CPU/GPU and exposes a standard OpenAI‑compatible HTTP API on the local network, eliminating cloud costs and data‑leak risks.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: OlliteRT turns an old Android phone into a private, offline LLM inference server, cutting API costs and eliminating data‑leak vectors.
final_briefs.who_cares: AI developers, mobile engineers, and privacy‑focused teams prototyping on‑device intelligence.

final_briefs.title: SSH Is the Most Underrated Platform in Tech
final_briefs.description: **SSH is a full‑featured remote‑access platform that most developers only scratch the surface of.** Beyond login, SSH provides tunneling, port forwarding, file transfer, key management and more, letting you replace ad‑hoc VPNs and custom scripts with a single, stable tool.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: SSH is a full‑featured remote‑access platform—tunneling, port‑forwarding, and secret‑management—that can replace ad‑hoc VPNs and custom scripts.
final_briefs.who_cares: DevOps, backend engineers, and site‑reliability engineers who regularly move traffic or data across firewalls.

final_briefs.title: C# Features I Wish I Had When I Started in 2016
final_briefs.description: **Modern C# additions like top‑level statements and raw string literals cut boilerplate dramatically.** Features introduced from C# 9 through C# 15—target‑typed new, raw string literals, the field keyword, and labeled break/continue—let you write clearer, more concise code compared to legacy WebForms patterns.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: New C# syntactic sugar—top‑level statements, target‑typed new, raw string literals—drastically reduces boilerplate and makes code clearer.
final_briefs.who_cares: .NET developers, especially those maintaining legacy codebases or writing CLI utilities.
